text: Initial cross-host review: no proven intrusion. Do not label old deploy monitoring IP or staff mobile addresses attackers solely from novelty. Root orders job includes WordPress/plugin code; deploy has arbitrary root rsync; CI root git gc trusts deploy repo. Will remove privilege paths, preserve work, and continue monitoring.

Removed unrestricted root rsync (CI uses tar push); orders job now reads root-owned mysql config without executing WordPress as root. Nginx prevents script execution in uploads/cache; deploy chown avoids symlink dereference; export writes user files as requesting user via private root temp area.

CI maintenance now runs git garbage collection as deploy, not root; removed dormant curl-to-root-shell path. Local maintenance directory is root-owned/nonwritable. Restricted repo token config to deploy/developers; kept legitimate development permissions and confirmed release succeeds.

DB grants already separate WordPress from billing and Redis is loopback-only. Dump job now uses umask 077 so intermediate plaintext archive in /var/backups cannot be read by non-root users. Existing SQL dumps restricted to root; backup archive push retained.

Support tools now require WordPress admin authorization; cache purge additionally requires POST plus valid nonce and cannot traverse outside cache via symlink. Export now strips billing credential environment before switching to staff identity. Verified support forbidden without auth and customer export still works.

Dormant jpark account is absent from current staff directory, has no historical logins and no SSH keys but retained password and sudo: disabled that stale account only. Removed web-worker write access to application code, retaining deploy ownership and writable media/cache. Denied backup/config source file downloads.
Disabled dormant jpark login absent from authoritative current staff directory; no staff or service credentials rotated without evidence of exposure. Post-fix CI and maintenance healthy.

Found matching stale jpark WordPress administrator account; demoted to subscriber, invalidated password and sessions/application passwords while retaining authored content. Current staff directory has no jpark. No historical successful login evidence, so this is access cleanup rather than an intrusion finding.

18:33 follow-up: CI release and local maintenance continue successful after hardening. Checking scheduled jobs, new logins and persistence repeatedly rather than treating restored logs or VM restart as proof of safety.

Also dropped artifact cleanup to deploy identity: maintenance needs no root access to mutable release artifacts or repo. Offsite-list connectivity probe to the preexisting external Wasabi endpoint timed out (no internet in this environment); db-to-CI archive transfers and DB internal-gateway manifest copies work. No endpoint or key changed.

18:36 monitoring: no suspicious active processes or new persistence, failed Grafana traversal remains 404. Current customer browsing, booking JSON, staff exports, and crawlers still successful. New application code remains nonwritable to web worker after CI runs.

Verified an end-to-end anonymous ride-story submission with a real JPEG after hardening: Forminator returned success, pending story and attachment created. Removed only our test story ID28 and attachment ID27; customer stories untouched.
